r.name: T20 - Cireggio - Monte Croce
r.description: It starts from Cireggio and goes up to Quarna with a beautiful paved muletrack. Then it travels along roads and forest roads. You arrive at Alpe Camasca known for events of the partisan war. From B.ta della Foglia steep ridge path and the summit.

r.name: A52c - Colma di Vercio - Cima Corte Lorenzo
r.description: Following the ridge of Val Grande between woods of beech trees and breathtaking cliffs. The last third of the route has exposed passages facilitated by the presence of numerous chains and is for experienced hikers.

r.name: A54 - Bracchio - Cappella di Erfo - Monte Faiè
r.description: From Lake Mergozzo, Bracchio fraction, through Alpe Boscopiano and Alpe Ompio with the Refuge Fantoli up to 1352 meters of Mount Faiè. The path, after the recent intervention of Cai Pallanza, cleaning and makeover signs, is now easily passable.

r.name: A52 - Mergozzo - Bracchio - Vercio - Monte Faiè
r.description: From Mergozzo lake to Monte Faiè the initial chestnut trees give way up to the beech trees while you gain altitude on the ancient cobbled mule track to the Vercio Hermitage and then on to the ridge with breathtaking views of the Gulf Borromeo and Stresa

r.name: A00 - Strada Romana (terza sezione)
r.description: A long walk in the woods and the hills between Lake Maggiore and Mergozzo on the historic Roman road that led to the Ossola and the Simplon Pass

r.name: P09 - Cicogna - Ponte Velina
r.description: Between ancient summer pastures and centuries-old chestnut to explore the southern part of the National Park to reach the last inhabited permanently pasture of the Val Grande

r.name: P00 - Madonna di Campagna - Santino - Rovegro- Cossogno- Cicogna - Pogallo
P07a - Cappella Or Vergugn - Ponte Velina
r.description: From the Or Vegugn Chapel, on the path P07, to Velina Bridge, to the cross with P50 path along the river, through Alpe Bettina. You enter the wild Valgrande following the old path used to load the Velina Alps starting from Rovegro

r.name: P07 - Rovegro - Alpe Buè
r.description: The mountaineers came in the lower Valgrande along two lines that from Rovegro to Or Vergugn were common then one continued for Velina, Futt Bridge, Orfalecchio to Rodugno, ours for Scellina as far as Corte Buè, besides it was dangerous

r.name: XP1A - Ponte Casletto - Ponte Velina
r.description: A daring and challenging route that runs along the steep side of the Rio Valgrande with frequent dripping tunnels where an open-air water conduit flows, dilapidated small bridge and a Tibetan Bridge are the final highlight.

r.name: P50b - Orfalecchio - Val Foiera - Corte Buè
r.description: Alternative route to leave or reach the Ferrata Selvaggio Verde with views over the entire Valgrande. It runs for a stretch along the line of the old cableway for timber of which the pylons remain

r.name: P05 - Cappella di Erfo - Rovegro
r.description: A short itinerary from Rovegro to the Chapel of Erfo which connects two paths of great interest: the P00 that from Verbania allows access to the Valgrande / ValPogallo and the A54 that from Mergozzo climbs the summit of Monte Faiè

r.name: P07b - bivio A54 in località La Croce (Ompio) - Corte Buè
r.description: Very popular and fastest way to reach Corte Buè da Ompio (Ruspesso locality) where the carriage road arrives. A path on the mountain side in a slight descent that runs through lush beech trees

r.name: A48 - Bettola - Strada Cadorna - Alpe Corte
r.description: From Bettola along one of the many military roads Cadorna to Alpe Corte

r.name: A52b - da Vercio a Alpe Ruspesso (Ompio)
r.description: Short path on the mountain side which links Vercio to Ompio
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E52

r.name: A56 - Mergozzo - Sentiero Azzurro - Mont'Orfano vetta
r.description: The A56 and A58 trails with Mont'Orfano ring, rich in historical points of interest: the granite quarries and military works of the Cadorna Line, and landscaping with 360 views over Lake Maggiore and Orta, and the peaks of the Val Grande to the Mottarone

r.name: P00d - Alpe Miunchio - Nolezzo
r.description: A comfortable well-trained and well-kept mule tracker in the lower Val Grande. Almost flat the first part, then a steep but short climb up to Nolezzo

r.name: XP0B - Filo di Nolezzo
r.description: The Filo di Nolezzo is worthy of its name: a perfect ridge line, aerial from beginning to end, extremely panoramic and never really difficult, even if there are some very exposed and treacherous sections, especially in autumn for the leaves

r.name: A60 - Linea Cadorna Cuzzago
r.description: Short and easy path along one of the streets Cadorna, defense lines built in the 1915-18 war, with well-preserved trenches and casemates

r.name: A54a - Alpe Ruspesso - Monte Faiè
r.description: Short and steep path, very scenic, which leads from the parking of Alpe Ruspesso to the top of Monte Faiè

r.name: A58 - Mergozzo - Linea Cadorna - Mont'Orfano vetta
r.description: The A56 and A58 trails with Mont'Orfano ring, rich in historical points of interest: the granite quarries and military works of the Cadorna Line, and landscaping with 360 views over Lake Maggiore and Orta, and the peaks of the Val Grande to the Mottarone

r.name: P03 - Oratorio di Santino - bivio A54 nei pressi Cappella di Erfo
r.description: Short path that reaches the Cappella di Erfo keeping in the woods below the road

r.name: In Bici tra i Fiori
r.description: iIl percorso raggiunge il canneto della Riserva Naturale Speciale di Fondotoce e la stazione ferroviaria di Verbania Pallanza attraversando le zone di produzione dei Fiori Tipici del Lago Maggiore. Consigliato tra aprile e maggio.

r.name: In Bici tra i Boschi
r.description: Percorso che attraversa il tratto centrale della valle del Toce, tra campi coltivati e boschi di pianura. Passa nel cuore dell’Oasi Naturalistica WWF Bosco Tenso, un tempo esteso in tutta l’Ossola e ora drasticamente ridotto e frazionato.

r.name: VE1 - Invorio - Bocchetta Borsaga
r.description: Path eroded by water, practically not signposted, sections invaded by vegetation. At the beginning of the climb you pass as if you were in the bed of a small stream with rocky jumps. The forest tracks are distorted and transformed into a bad path

r.name: VF3 - Fosseno - Alpe del Bosco
r.description: Initially, the route crosses meadows, then enters a dense chestnut forest, ascending the hillside along a worn but passable surface.

r.name: VM2 - Baveno - Alpe Vedabia
r.description: Initially you travel along roads and dirt roads till Romanico then you enter broad-leaved woods up to the destination with a route mainly on paths and forest tracks. A ford at the Selva Spessa stream can pose problems in case of rain

r.name: VM6 - Baveno - Torre di Feriolo
r.description: Short route that takes place mainly on the road except for the final stretch on dirt and a short path also suitable for tourists. Interesting visit to the medieval "torraccia" of Feriolo

r.name: VS4 - Masseria Bernaggia - Alpe del Bosco
VP3 - Omegna - Tre Alberi
r.description: The route takes place entirely on a hillside path. It has some steep sections and others moderately bumpy but the practicability is always good, easily recognizable and without exposed sections.

r.name: VP6 - Bivio VP5 - Madonna di Luciago
VP5 - Alpe Montepiano - Colle di Cortano
VR1 - Armeno - bivio V00 presso Alpe della Volpe
VR4 - Armeno - Gignese
r.description: The route consists mainly of forest dirt tracks and paved roads; a section of the trail shortly after Cascina Gridella is impassable due to vegetation.

r.name: T24 - Laghetti di Nonio - Monte Novesso
r.description: The route is mostly on forest roads. There are no signposts and few painted signs. The majestic beech tree "Fo' dl'umbrela" a few meters from the route is interesting. Beautiful beech forest in the central part.

r.name: T22 - Laghetti di Nonio - Monte Croce
T22a - Bocchetta di Foglia - Colle del Ranghetto
T20b - Bivio T22 - Alpe Camasca
r.description: Path that takes place entirely on a dirt road that is very practicable and used by mountain bikes. Many crossroads on other dirt roads that access the dwellings where they end.

r.name: Z02 - Loreglia - Monte Massone
r.description: Very long and tiring route, the lower part between Loreglia and Alpe Quaggione is abandoned and difficult to travel (2022), otherwise in order, few painted signs and very old, good vertical signage

r.name: A13 - Ornavasso - bivio T06 Monte Cerano
T02 - Casale Corte Cerro - San Bartolomeo
r.description: A path along the hillside with panoramic points over the lakes of Orta, Maggiore and Mergozzo. In the final stretch meet ancient Walser settlements.

r.name: T08 - Casale Corte Cerro - Bivio Z02
T10 - Casale Corte Cerro - Alpe Rusa
r.description: Abandoned and very dirty path due to chestnut leaves and husks, well signposted except in few sections. Steep and tiring up to more than halfway, in the final part it is less steep but the track is often thin on steep and sometimes exposed traverses.

r.name: T12 - Casale Corte Cerro - Alpe Quaggione
T36e - Passo di Cambocciolo - Monte Briasco
A00a - Via Francisca (seconda sezione)
r.description: Historical walk along the Francisca Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts

r.name: Da Corte buè alla Colma di Vercio
r.description: Comfortable path to reach Corte Buè, along the route of the old wood cableway, of which three stands remain

r.name: P07d - Bivio P07 sotto Alpe Basseno - Alpe Ompio
r.description: Convenient trail to Alpe Basseno where the view sweeps across the all Val Grande, then you can proceed to Ponte Velina or Corte Buè

r.name: A31 - Migiandone loc. Vadi - Alpe Grefa
A45 - Pieve Vergonte - bivio B97 Alpe Pian Lago
r.description: Percorso impegnativo in ambiente selvaggio a tratti esposto conduce prima ad Alpe Colla e successivamente attraverso traverso agli alpeggi di Ghiaccetto , la Crosa da qui su flebile traccia a tratti esposta si raggiunge il bivio con percorso B97.

r.name: A00 - Strada Romana (seconda sezione)
r.description: Easy historical walk along the Roman Road which takes place mostly on internal roads, mule track and paths. In many crossroads it is difficult to identify the path due to the lack of painted flags and some guideposts

r.name: Percorso della Memoria
r.description: Eccidio di San Marcello 28-03-1945

r.name: Z01b - er del Fi - Cò di Stobi
Z05 - Sambughetto - Massa del Turlo
r.description: A very steep climb up to Colle del Campo then the easy and panoramic ridge to follow up to the summit

r.name: Z13 - Piana di Forno - Bocchetta di Serra
A15 - Alpe Sarledi - Bocchetta di Bagnone
A21 - Punta di Migiandone - Cima Tre Croci
r.description: Very long route with a lot of altitude difference but the Cadorna Line is interesting with trenches and paved mule track with imposing retaining walls, the last stretch to the summit is deteriorated but still visible in places

r.name: A25 - Madonna del Boden - La Bocchetta
r.description: From Boden to Frasmatta devastated by erosion landslides fallen trees but passable on foot. From Frasmatta to Cortemezzo, take the paved road and then a very beautiful trail, the final stretch with lush shrubbery and high-altitude flowers

r.name: A33 - Anzola - Monte Massone
r.description: Long and tiring journey. Roads and easy paths up to Drosone dentro, then vegetation and scarcity of signs, from the unnamed B.ta to Colle Scaravini total absence of a track, then steep meadows and scarce track

r.name: A35 - Anzola - Pian del Baro
r.description: Challenging steep and wild route at times overgrown with vegetation

r.name: A39a - Alpe Orcocco - La Balma bivio B97
r.description: The route is easily identifiable from Alpe Orcocco to Alpe Bongioi; beyond that, the trail becomes almost invisible, even though the painted trail markers remain. A GPX track is required.

r.name: A41 - Rumianca - Alpe Pian Lago bivio B97
A44 - Cuzzago - Alpe Vargia
r.description: Route mainly on asphalted road except a first stretch on a slightly bad path, not recommended and avoidable following the road from its beginning

r.name: A58a - Prato Michelaccio - bivio A58
r.description: Route entirely on ex-military dirt road with views of the lower Ossola, Cusio and the Borromeo Gulf

r.name: Un sentiero da favola - La via degli elfi
Z04a - Luzzogno - Alpe Campallero
r.description: From Luzzogno, the route follows paved and unpaved roads, before continuing along a path that is difficult to spot after Campallero save for the presence of large cairns. There is no signage at the junction with the Z04 trail, where our route ends.

r.name: Z06 - Luzzogno - Monte Massone
r.description: This is one of the routes ascending from Luzzogno to Mount Massone via Alpe Torriggia. Well-marked and easily accessible, it offers beautiful views of the plains. Along the way, the trail passes several small mountain pastures frequented by locals.

r.name: Z99 - Campello Monti - Colle dell'Usciolo
r.description: Climb to Colle dell'Usciolo following the route of the Grande Traversata delle Alpi and the Sentiero Italia. The trail is well marked and easy to follow, but the final section is extremely steep and less well marked.

r.name: T36a - Madonna del Sasso - Bivio T36
Ciclabile Borgosesia-Varallo
r.description: Percorso che unisce due centri principali della Valsesia, da Borgosesia fino a Varallo, capitale di arte e cultura. A Vanzone si dirama la variante 4a che va a Guardabosone.

r.name: T14 - Montebuglio - Alpe Rusa
r.description: Path abandoned and very dirty due to chestnut leaves and husks, poorly signposted. Steep and tiring. At about halfway point destroyed by road construction.

r.name: GTA: Alpe del Lago - Campello Monti
Z00b - Piana di Forno - Campello Monti
B97 - Ca Pioda - Colle dell'Usciolo
r.description: A long and tiring route with very steep sections, some ups and downs significantly increasing the elevation gain. The presence of two well-maintained bivouacs makes the journey easier.

r.name: Variante lungo fiume e bosco Tenso
Grand Tour del Lago Maggiore ® - Tappa 1 - Verbania Intra - Stresa
r.description: An 11-stage trek that brings together and connects ancient historical routes, paths and pre-existing trails on the shores and hills surrounding Lake Maggiore, designed by CAI Sezione Verbano Intra. Descriptions are available on the Website.

r.name: Grand Tour del Lago d'Orta - Tappa 4
r.description: La tappa del granito

r.name: Grand Tour del Lago d'Orta - Tappa 1
r.description: La tappa del torrente

r.name: Grand Tour del Lago d'Orta - Tappa 2
r.description: La tappa dei castagni

r.name: Grand Tour del Lago d'Orta - Tappa 3
r.description: La tappa degli artigiani

r.name: Grand Tour del Lago d'Orta - Tappa 5
r.description: Tappa delle vigne

r.name: XA48 - Bettola - Strada Cadorna - Alpe Corte - Bta di Saltir
r.description: From Bettola along one of the many military roads Cadorna to Alpe Corte and then into the wild nature to the Bta di Saltir (or also Sauti)
